architecture.summary: The complete S1-01/S1-02/S1-03a stack retires customer grant writes and uses two hosted roles: User gives product/MCP access; Admin includes that access and administration. Current active memberships and validated role catalogs authorize requests. Default, retired, unknown, inactive, missing, and foreign grants cannot authorize access. Administration has no MFA precondition, and legacy inferred MFA values normalize to false while session/cookie formats remain compatible. Active product-member counts include each unique authorized membership once. The stack introduces neutral identity session/profile and signup contracts. Named signup requires canonical organization-purpose documents and a verified creator. A confirmed new organization and reread must match its name, identity, and ten-field v2 authority/legal record before the initial Admin write. The membership response and a current read must confirm that Admin/product access. Retained v1/v2 records are read-only replay barriers; they cannot restore grants or convert personal consent. The signup route selects the confirmed organization, preserves cookie ordering and cancellation, then opens its MCP guide. A neutral callback supplies the exact active-membership name to portal JSON; missing names fail safely and names render as text. CSRF/origin checks, bounded admission, safe failures, native invitations, and browser/MCP organization isolation remain. The unchanged personal production bundle cannot enable new creation; approved organization wording and live cutover checks remain S1-05. No provider setting, new datastore, infrastructure, SDK dependency, or resource lifetime changes. The registry records these component/runtime guarantees; existing parent diagrams remain accurate. The web-to-organizations owner pair is declared runtime because the form calls its public name validator; forbidden edges and the declared public-module list remain. Signup adapter tests move to integration for that real collaboration. Required gate selection and approval rules remain; the image assertion now checks the legacy-bundle refusal. Observable authorization, persistence, and portal/server contracts require T2 Need architect. Internal interfaces, sensitive paths, the dependency declaration, and retained quality findings also require human review. No new decision record was requested. The stack includes the shared developer metrics repair from PR #230. Portal access and organization-name specifications now have separate files with unchanged scenarios and assertions. Application boundaries and numeric review goals remain unchanged.
